note: Literature explicitly explores genotype-phenotype divergence in BRD4 alterations, comparing point missense variants affecting histone binding with haploinsufficiency and contiguous deletions.

evidence.text: BRD4 haploinsufficiency from deletions results in a CdLS-like or contiguous gene presentation, while point missense mutations have been linked to classical presentations via altered chromatin interaction.

source.title: Confirmation of BRD4 haploinsufficiency role in Cornelia de Lange–like phenotype and delineation of a 19p13.12p13.11 gene contiguous syndrome
source.quote: We report a new 19p deletion in a patient clinically diagnosed as CdLS, partially overlapping with previously published cases with the aim to support the role of BRD4 haploinsufficiency in a CdL-like phenotype and to improve the delineation of 19p13.12p13.11 deletion as a new nonrecurrent gene contiguous syndrome

evidence.text: An international cohort study of 14 patients evaluated the phenotypic spectrum across variant classes including large deletions, null variants, and missense variants, showing recognizable phenotypes within cohesinopathies.

source.title: Understanding the new BRD4‐related syndrome: Clinical and genomic delineation with an international cohort study
source.quote: We formed an international collaborative study, and collected 14 new patients, including two fetuses. We performed phenotype and genotype analysis, integrated prenatal findings from fetopathological examinations, phenotypes of pediatric patients and adults.
